 Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant/ claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the judgment dated 14.01.2020 passed in MVC No.1160/2018 of XI Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional MACT, Belagavi.

entities.text: MVC No.1160/2018 of XI Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional MACT, Belagavi
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 2. The appellant/ petitioner has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident which took place on 27.07.2017.
He made a claim petition claiming compensation.

The Tribunal after recording the evidence has awarded compensation as under:
Towards pain and suffering : Rs. 50,000-00 Towards loss of amenities : Rs.
50,000-00 and enjoyment in life Towards loss of future : Rs. 3,06,000-00 income
Towards medical expenses : Rs. 1,24,290-00 and incidental charges
Towards attendant's charges, : Rs. 13,500-00 food, nourishment and conveyance expenses Towards loss of income : Rs. 60,000-00 during period of treatment
The appellant/ claimant is seeking enhancement of compensation as awarded by the Tribunal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.2/
insurance company.
5.

The counsel for appellant would contend that the accident occurred in the year 2017 and as per the chart prepared by the Legal Services Authority for settlement of disputes in Lok-Adalat is 10,250/- and the Tribunal ought to have taken the said amount.
He contends that the injured has sustained comminuted displaced fracture of proximal end of the right tibia with vascular compromised with neuropraxia right great toe.
Considering the said aspect, PW.2-Doctor has given disability of 50% of right lower limb and Tribunal has erred in taking the disability of full body of 15%.

Shri.Ramakrishna Gangaram Kumbar vs Shri.Parashuram Arjun Kumbar on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21052902/
2 6.

entities.text: Shri.Ramakrishna Gangaram Kumbar vs Shri.Parashuram Arjun Kumbar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that the appellant is a mason and the said injury has affected his working as mason and prays to take functional disability as 25%.

He submits that NC: 2024:KHC-D:14181 the compensation awarded under other heads i.e., pain and suffering, loss of amenities, attendant charges are on the lower side, with this he prayed to allow the appeal.

7. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would contend that the Tribunal has rightly taken the disability of the whole body at 15%, taking into consideration the evidence of the Doctor who has stated 50% of disability towards right lower limb.
He contends that the compensation awarded for pain and suffering, loss of amenities and attendant charges are just and proper.
He contends that loss of income during laid up period awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side, with this he prayed to dismiss the appeal.
8. Having heard the learned counsels, the Court has perused the impugned judgment and award and other materials placed on record.
9. The accident has occurred in the year 2017 and the appellant/ claimant is aged 28 years working as mason NC: 2024:KHC-D:14181 is not in dispute.

The Tribunal has taken the income of the injured at 10,000/- per month, as per the chart prepared by Legal Services Authority for settlement of disputes for Lok-Adalat, the notional income fixed for the year 2017 is 10,250/-, the Tribunal ought to have taken the said income.

10. PW.2, the Doctor who has treated the injured/ claimant has stated that the injured has sustained comminuted displaced fracture of proximal end of the right tibia with vascular compromised with neuropraxia right great toe and he has assessed disability to the extent of 50% to the right lower limb.

Considering the aspect of petitioner/ claimant is a mason and the said injury has affected his functioning as a mason, the Tribunal ought to have taken the disability at 20% instead of 15%.
11.
In view of the above, the compensation for loss of the future income is (10,250  12  17  20/100) 4,18,200/-.
Considering the fracture sustained with neuropraxia right great toe, the compensation awarded NC: 2024:KHC-D:14181 towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities are on lower side.

The claimant is entitled 60,000/- towards pain and suffering and 60,000/-
towards loss of amenities.
The Tribunal has rightly awarded the medical expenses in a sum of 1,24,290.
The claimant was admitted in the Hospital for 33 days and therefore, he is entitled to attendant charges, food and nourishment charges in a sum of 33,000/-(33 x 1,000).
The loss of income during laid up period as awarded by the Tribunal in a sum of 60,000/- is on the higher side.
The appellant/ claimant is entitled to loss of income during laid up period in a sum of 30,750/-(10,250 x 3 months).

12. In view of the above, the appellant/ claimant is entitled to compensation as under:
Medical expenses : Rs. 1,24,290-00

Pain and sufferings : Rs. 60,000-00 Loss of Future Amenities : Rs. 60,000-00 Attendant, Food and : Rs. 33,000-00 Nourishment charges Loss of Future Income : Rs. 4,18,200-00 Loss of Income during Laid : Rs. 30,750-00 Up period Total : Rs. 7,26,240-00 NC:
Shri.Ramakrishna Gangaram Kumbar vs Shri.Parashuram Arjun Kumbar on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21052902/
3 2024:KHC-D:14181 13.

The appellant/ claimant is entitled to total compensation of 7,26,240/- as against 6,03,790/-
as awarded by the Tribunal.

In view of the above, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

ii) The appellant is entitled to total compensation of 7,26,240/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
iii) The respondent No.2 - insurance company shall deposit the compensation with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment, failing which, it is liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:14181 iv) The appellant is entitled to release of entire amount of compensation.

Sd/-
